content.text:
I matched the barcode against all ten videos. Using ffmpeg, I took one frame per second from each video and shrank it to its average colour. I then stretched each sequence to the barcode's width and measured the mean colour difference along the middle row of the barcode (lower means a closer match).

| Option | Video | Mean difference |
|---|---|---|
| **G** | **twenty one pilots – Stressed Out** | **17.2** |
| B | Alan Walker – Faded | 26.6 |
| F | Clean Bandit – Rockabye | 27.5 |
| J | Sia – Chandelier | 27.9 |
| E | Linkin Park – Numb | 29.8 |
| I | Taylor Swift – Blank Space | 34.0 |
| D | Coldplay – Hymn for the Weekend | 35.5 |
| C | twenty one pilots – Heathens | 37.1 |
| H | Imagine Dragons – Thunder | 38.9 |
| A | Imagine Dragons – Believer | 41.4 |

Stressed Out is clearly the best match, about 9 points ahead of the next video. That fits the barcode's muted grey look. The comparison is rough, though: it uses a single row of pixels and lines the timing up evenly. I didn't check individual frames by eye.

Answer: G
